## Evidence and current boundary defects

Read the complete proposal `docs/build/raffle-admission-minimum-fee-20261007.md`, the user instructions, relevant R3 gates, the complete raffle contract, chain types/ports/actions/reader/service/workflow/fee and seller helpers, wallet session and WalletConnect provider, transaction review component, relevant seller/public workspace, current and historical terms linkage, deployment attestation, and prior Claude source review. Prior assurances were treated as hypotheses.

1. `LabxRaffle.sol:_open` currently checks only the cached escrow flag and has no LABx admission gate. Both selectors reach it. Direct callers bypass any website curation. Require the approval, code and current custody checks below. Verification must call both selectors directly.
2. `refund`, `claimFee`, `fees.ts:sellerAccounting`, `actions.ts` refund amount, `workflow.ts` refund availability, and `RaffleWorkspace.tsx` refundable balance all encode the superseded fee-refund policy. Keeping even one consumer unchanged produces incorrect liabilities or repeated unusable refund actions. Verification must exercise refund and treasury payout in both orders and then reload both buyer and seller views.
3. `service.ts:submit/confirm/resume` assumes direct EOA transactions. It obtains the account transaction count, forces that nonce, requires the outer transaction sender to equal the connected account and compares direct raffle calldata. A Safe execution has an outer executor transaction and a Safe call. Reusing this logic for Safe approvals will reject valid executions or strand the pending journal. Implement the narrow owner path below. Do not relax existing financial confirmation checks.
4. `RaffleWorkspace.tsx` deliberately denies operator access to the seller workspace, and seller action filtering excludes operator controls. Owner review therefore needs its own small route/component. Do not weaken seller isolation.
5. Published terms say mainnet is disabled although the constructor rejects only chain 1, use transaction instead of purchase-call rounding, and promise fee refunds. Correct current v3 text as specified below. Do not rewrite archived v2 text.

## Exact contract interface

Keep `RaffleView/getRaffle`, lifecycle selector names and contract version 3. Append `uint256 minBuyerFeeUsdc` to `RafflePolicy`. Add `uint256 public constant MIN_BUYER_FEE_USDC = 2_500_000`; this is a compile-time immutable value, not a configurable fee. `_openingPolicy` includes it and `_quote` consumes the pinned value.

Add these selectors, using ABI-derived frontend types:

```solidity
function draftReviewHash(uint256 id) public view returns (bytes32);
function getRaffleAdmission(uint256 id) external view returns (RaffleAdmission memory);
function approveRaffle(uint256 id, bytes32 expectedReviewHash) external;
function revokeRaffleApproval(uint256 id, bytes32 expectedReviewHash) external;
```

The minimal returned admission record has `uint256 reviewRevision`, `bytes32 approvedReviewHash`, `address approvedBy`, and `bool approvedAtOpening`. Expose the current `ownerGeneration` and `openingPolicyGeneration` as public uint256 values. `draftReviewHash` requires an existing Draft and hashes current bounded data. It does not call untrusted NFT functions. Frontend readers derive current validity by comparing the stored approval with this hash; a hash match alone is not a custody guarantee. Avoid adding a permanently ambiguous generic `approved` boolean.

Store review revision per raffle and frozen approval record separately from `RaffleView`. Start each draft revision at 1. Increment on every successful `_setDraft`, even identical inputs or edits later reversed. Increment on revocation too. Escrow need not change the revision because approval requires escrow and NFT identity locks on escrow; include the escrow flag in the hash. The revision never decreases. Solidity checked arithmetic must remain enabled.

Use `keccak256(abi.encode(...))`, with a fixed domain tag, to bind chain ID, raffle contract, raffle ID, seller, NFT contract, token ID, NFT runtime code hash, escrow flag, title, salesEnd, reserveNonce, reserveCommit, pack count, each ordered pack's name/price/bonusEntries/maxSupply/active, reviewRevision, owner address, ownerGeneration, openingPolicyGeneration and `openingPolicyHash()`. Bound loops by existing MAX_PACKS. Hash strings/arrays with canonical ABI encoding, not ambiguous packed concatenation. Existing sold counters are zero in Draft and are not editable inputs. The full policy hash includes coordinator, treasury, terms, key hash, subscription, callback gas, confirmations, billing mode, both fee rates and the minimum.

Increment `openingPolicyGeneration` on every successful setter of a field in `_openingPolicy`, including setter calls that restore prior values or set identical values: `setTreasury`, `setTermsHash`, `setVrfConfig`, `setNativePayment`, and successful `applyCoordinator`. The proposal of a coordinator alone does not change current policy. Increment `ownerGeneration` on every `acceptOwnership`, including transfer away and back. Merely setting `pendingOwner` does not transfer current authority. Pause and ETH enablement are existing operational controls, not additions to the pinned policy, so their toggles do not silently add new invalidation semantics.

Both approval mutations require current owner, Draft, and expectedReviewHash equal to the live draft hash. Approval also requires r.escrowed, nonempty NFT code, `ownerOf(tokenId) == address(this)` and a future salesEnd. Store the digest and msg.sender. Emit `RaffleApproved(uint256 indexed id, address indexed approver, bytes32 indexed reviewHash)`.

Revocation requires an existing stored approval, even if it is stale. It clears stored approval hash/address and increments reviewRevision before emitting `RaffleApprovalRevoked(uint256 indexed id, address indexed approver, bytes32 indexed reviewHash, uint256 nextRevision)`, where reviewHash is the pre-revocation current review hash supplied by the caller. Requiring the expected current hash stops an old revoke transaction from invalidating a newly reviewed draft. Incrementing the revision prevents an old pending approve transaction from reinstating a revoked approval. Draft edits may retain the previous approval record so the UI can distinguish changed from never reviewed; validity always uses the live hash. Repeated approval of an already matching digest may be idempotent. No repeated approve operation grants another draw.

Inside shared `_open`, require stored approvedBy equal to current owner, stored nonzero digest equal to `draftReviewHash(id)`, nonempty NFT code, and current `ownerOf(tokenId) == address(this)`. Preserve seller, Draft, pause and time checks. Then pin the policy, set approvedAtOpening true, and open. `openWithPolicy` keeps its existing expected-policy check; plain `open` gets the same mandatory admission enforcement. Reverting NFT reads fail closed. No approval mutation is permitted after Draft. Later ownership, policy, code or approval changes must not add a gate to buy/draw/reveal/settle/claims/cancel/recovery. The approval record becomes historical once opened.

Use nonReentrant for both new mutators, following the existing lifecycle entrypoints. Do not introduce external mutable calls into hash calculation. The owner identity and epochs must still match at actual transaction execution, including delayed Safe execution.

## Money invariants and events

For each successful purchase call, principal equals selected pack price times quantity. Fee equals `max(pinnedMinimum, floor(principal * pinnedBuyerBps / 10_000))`. One call selects one pack ID. Separate calls, including calls in one smart-wallet batch, each pay their own minimum. A reverted call transfers and credits nothing. Principal is always positive for a valid purchase.

For USDC purchases, read the contract balance before and after safeTransferFrom and require an exact increase of principal plus fee before `_credit`. Explicitly reject a decrease or different delta with a clear receipt error. A fee-on-transfer mock, zero-transfer success mock and anomalous over-delivery must revert atomically. The existing ETH path may continue accepting at least the requested USDC amount; any excess is unallocated surplus. Both routes credit only the quoted amount. This assumes the token reports balances honestly and does not protect against a wholly malicious or confiscating token.

`principalOf[id][buyer]` remains the outstanding principal entitlement in cancellation. `feeOf[id][buyer]` becomes cumulative processing fees actually paid by that buyer. Document that it is historical, never a refund entitlement; do not clear it on refund. `_buyerFees` is likewise cumulative collected processing fees. `getRaffleAccounting` remains cumulative, including cancelled/refunded purchases. Neither counter changes when fees are withdrawn.

`refund` requires Cancelled and positive caller principal. Zero principal reverts even when feeOf is positive. Zero principalOf, subtract principalEscrow only, transfer that principal in USDC, and emit existing `Refunded(id,buyer,principal)` only. Never read feeOf to calculate a refund, and never decrease feeEscrow in refund. Failed transfer rolls back those effects. Refund succeeds independently of treasury payment, NFT recovery or another blocked recipient.

`claimFee` remains permissionless and pays the pinned `_policies[id].treasury`, never msg.sender or current global treasury. Permit only Settled or Cancelled with positive feeEscrow. Zero feeEscrow before transfer, preserve rollback on transfer failure, and emit existing FeeClaimed with the actual payout. In Cancelled it contains only retained processing fees. A cancelled never-opened draft has zero fees; reject zero claims before looking up its unpinned treasury. No fee claims in Open, Closed, Drawing or Drawn.

`settle` keeps the existing one-time commission based on gross principal. It moves floor(gross * sellerBps / 10_000) from principalEscrow to feeEscrow. No cancellation path applies seller commission. Preserve current Settled event semantics: principal is seller net, fee is processing fees plus commission. Terminal phases remain disjoint.

At all times, per-raffle principalEscrow plus feeEscrow equals credited receipts minus successful transfers for that raffle. The token balance must cover the sum of all raffle liabilities; surplus is not claimable. For cancelled raffles refund liability is principalEscrow only. Refunded principal is cumulative gross less current principalEscrow. Retained fees equal cumulative buyerFees, regardless of treasury claim. Remove refundedBuyerFees or set it explicitly to zero only if an existing consumer needs the field. Protocol fees paid equals buyerFees minus feeEscrow when Cancelled, and buyerFees plus commission minus feeEscrow when Settled. Never infer refunded fees from a treasury withdrawal.

Frontend helper becomes `buyerFee(principal, buyerFeeBps, minBuyerFeeUsdc)` with explicit validated bigint minimum and no fallback for active raffles. Reader quote, action allowance, ETH output/cap, buyer review, membership cards, dashboard and fixtures must use the same pinned data. Refund amount and availability depend only on principal. Historical fee display can remain after refund but must say nonrefundable processing fee paid.

## Bounded frontend and owner journey

Add an owner review route with a paged queue and a single-raffle review page, for example `/review` and `/review/[id]`. Reuse the existing WalletGate and existing maximum 24-ID catalog scan; filter Draft within each bounded page and retain a next cursor even for empty filtered pages. No unbounded scan to manufacture a complete queue. Untrusted NFT metadata failure must not prevent review data, revocation or the remainder of the queue.

Add admission data to pinned raffle reads or a dedicated `readAdmission({id,block})` result, with the same final block-hash check as readRaffle. Obtain draft digest, epochs, current policy, current owner, packs and custody at one block. Post-open reads use the frozen approval record and pinned policy; do not recompute Draft-only hashes. Check current custody separately and display failures as unknown/not held. Do not perform arbitrary ownerOf calls for every catalog item merely to show admission status.

Owner review shows the exact chain, raffle contract/ID, seller, NFT contract/token and explorer links, current custody owner, code hash, revision/digest, sales end, pack economics, commitment hashes, terms, treasury, coordinator, key hash, subscription, billing mode, callback gas/confirmations and fees. Require an explicit review of canonical collection provenance, transfer restrictions/upgradability and draw-funding use before preparing approval. These attestations are human review prompts, not an automated authenticity oracle. Do not expose private commercial commitment plaintext or grant access to seller private records.

Add workflow actions `approveRaffle` and `revokeRaffleApproval`, both containing id and expectedReviewHash. Require current connected account equal to on-chain owner, Draft and matching review hash in action construction and again immediately before submission. An EOA that is a Safe signer is not the Safe account. Existing action simulation may use the actual Safe as eth_call account. Add the selectors to normal EOA workflow recovery only where the existing direct-transaction assumptions hold. Seller controls remain separate; after escrow show Pending review, Changed since review or Approved from actual state, and allow open only with matching admission plus existing checks. Draft editing remains available and warns that it requires a fresh approval.

Safe execution needs a bounded special case for these two zero-value owner actions. Keep the existing financial service/journal confirmation rules intact. Never supply an EOA transaction-count nonce for a Safe proposal and never call a Safe proposal hash an executed transaction hash. A submitted proposal, pending signatures and chain execution are distinct states. Persist the deployment/owner/id/action/digest/review block intent if an automatic owner submission path is implemented.

Acceptable first interface, confirmed by parent: after simulation and review, provide the exact `{chainId, from: owner, to: raffle, value: 0, data}` payload and an explicit external Safe execution step. The owner completes the multisig flow in Safe, then supplies an execution transaction hash or refreshes a bounded event search. This is an external Safe step, not automatic WalletConnect execution. The existing WalletConnect account remains usable for identity and review. An automatic adapter may replace this only after its actual provider protocol and pending behavior are verified from current primary documentation and local tests.

For owner execution confirmation require a successful canonical receipt with the configured confirmation depth, an event emitted by the exact raffle contract matching action, raffle ID, approver and expected digest, and canonical post-receipt admission state. Approval success requires the matching stored hash/approver and unchanged relevant generations; if later edited/revoked/transferred, report executed but stale, not ready to open. Revocation confirmation matches its event including nextRevision; subsequent reapproval must not be mislabeled as still revoked. Do not require outer tx.from to equal the Safe and do not trust a snapshot alone. Unknown Safe hashes, missing events, wrong raffles, failed inner calls, reorgs and unrelated receipts must not complete the action. A refresh that discovers a matching chain event may say approval is recorded, without claiming this browser submitted it.

## Terms and trust assumptions

Update current v3 wording and derived terms hash everywhere it is pinned in fixtures. The fee is the greater of 2.50 USDC and 2% of principal per purchase call. State rounding in 0.000001-USDC units, one pack ID per call, quantity multiplication first and a new minimum for each split call. Cancellation returns principal only, even for draw timeout or funding failure; the successful purchase processing fee is retained. ETH-route refunds are principal denominated in USDC, not ETH; gas and swap costs are not refunded. Failed purchases retain no fee.

State that LABx approval covers the exact prize and use of draw funding, and seller draft edits require review again. Approval does not reserve subscription balance, guarantee transferability or prove authenticity. The operator can change future opening settings, cancel drafts/eligible no-sale raffles, reveal a valid commitment, pause new sales, and affect subscription funding. Existing permissionless recovery remains available, with the disclosed principal-only refund. Keep the exact existing cancellation conditions; do not grant a new discretionary cancellation right after sales.

Narrow the network statement to Ethereum mainnet chain 1 being blocked by the contract; the website permits only its approved Sepolia/local deployment modes. No constructor allowlist expansion is required for this amendment. Runtime attestation establishes bytecode/payment-token identity, not approved Safe custody, legitimate coordinator or NFT authenticity. Prior Claude authority/coordinator attestation findings remain a future-registration gate while APPROVED_DEPLOYMENTS is empty. Source UI must not imply those facts are automatically verified. Maintain the empty registry.

The owner must operationally reject deceptive/restrictable NFTs. A code hash does not capture proxy implementation or mutable transfer rules; a malicious ownerOf can lie. This design adds explicit admission, not proof of authenticity or a post-settlement transfer guarantee. It deliberately preserves independent payouts and adds no payout redirection or escrow adapter. Distinct raffles still have no guaranteed VRF budget reservation. These are disclosed limits, not waived implementation checks.

## Ownership and required verification

Use one isolated critical owner for `contracts/src/LabxRaffle.sol`, contract tests, generated ABI plus `web/lib/chain/abi.ts`, ABI-derived types, minimum helper, reader/actions/workflow/service boundary and any new owner submission/confirmation module. Include shared ports and the smallest controller needed to prove the journey. This slice changes authorization and financial accounting; do not assign those decisions to a mechanical worker. The critical owner also owns `web/lib/published-terms.ts` and its hash fixtures. Root owns integration, docs, static informational page copy and lockfiles, and coordinates wording before the critical owner pins the final terms hash.

After that API is fixed, an isolated Sol UI owner can implement review routes/components, admission status, fee/refund presentation, and mobile states against the committed interfaces. The UI owner must not change contract hashes, generation semantics, money calculations or transaction-confirmation rules. Serialize edits to existing RaffleWorkspace and TransactionFlow with the critical owner. Independent verification owns adversarial tests and browser evidence; send the matrix below to that engineer. No verification engineer was active in this review session, so parent receives the handoff.

Mandatory tests before final review:

- Principal 1 atomic unit; below/at/above 125-USDC crossover including micro-unit rounding; quantities 1 and 20; max price/qty; separate calls versus one quantity purchase; two calls in one smart-wallet batch; ETH parity and failed swap/refund rollback.
- Exact-receipt USDC under-delivery, zero delivery, over-delivery and failed transfers; multiple raffles plus unrelated surplus; aggregate liabilities through varied claim orders.
- Every cancellation path: draft/no sales, timed Open, timed Closed, empty snapshot where reachable, VRF abort. Refund before/after treasury, multiple buyers, double/zero-principal attempts while historical feeOf remains positive, blocked payee retry/isolation, no cancellation commission, no preterminal treasury claim, treasury stays pinned after global changes.
- Both opening selectors and direct calls: missing/revoked/wrong-owner/stale approval, absent or lost custody, NFT with no code, draft edit and restoration, every policy setter and restoration, owner A to B to A, stale approve queued before revoke, stale revoke queued before edit, expiry. Unknown raffle approval fails.
- Post-open owner/treasury/policy/approval mutations cannot invalidate admission or change pinned terms, amounts, draw, winner, refunds or claims. Every new mutator rejects all later phases. Seller still cancels an unapproved Draft and reclaims the prize.
- Pinned reader reorg rejection and bounded owner queue; missing metadata/custody-read failures; wrong wallet/chain; stale review between prepare/sign/execute; reload recovery. Existing financial confirmation tests continue unchanged.
- Owner review through recorded execution to seller opening in desktop/mobile browser. For Safe, use an executor address different from the Safe and an outer Safe call. Require matching actual raffle events and state; reject proposal-only hashes, missing/wrong events, failed inner execution, stale generation and reorg. An external-Safe first interface needs browser coverage of exact exported payload and verified execution-hash reconciliation, without claiming a live wallet test.
- Full existing contract regression/fuzz suites, web tests/typecheck/build, generated ABI agreement, historical v2 terms hash unchanged, registry empty, and EIP-170 runtime bytecode size. New hash/generation logic adds code near an already size-sensitive contract.

Required future gates remain independent behavioral verification, fresh Astra candidate review, actual Claude review of changed contract and final website, and the task's prior website/audit/cleanup acceptance. None ran here. No main push or on-chain deployment is authorized by this verdict. Next action: parent adopts this contract and assigns the isolated critical implementation, with the Safe interface choice explicit.
